Description: Mean Well's 350W slim-line 48V supply (350.4W rated, 7.3A) in a 220 × 62 × 31 mm fanless metal case with 94% efficiency and active PFC. It cools silently by convection with no fan, but must be mounted to an aluminium plate or cabinet base to meet its derating curve. A silent 350W option for 48V printer builds only — it cannot power a standard 24V board.
Verdict Label: Silent 350W supply for 48V builds — zero fan noise, but 48V boards only
Cons:
48V output — only for 48V-capable boards, not a drop-in for 24V printers
Must be mounted to an aluminium plate to meet its derating curve
Derates above ~45°C at 230VAC input
No DC OK signal or redundant function on the standard type
Name: UHP-350-48
Pros:
Silent fanless convection cooling, zero fan noise
350.4W / 7.3A at 48V
Slim 31mm profile — 220 × 62 × 31 mm
94% efficient with built-in active PFC
UL 62368-1 certified

Description: The LRS-100-24 is the compact variant of the Mean Well LRS family, right-sized for Voron V0 builds without a full-power bed upgrade, secondary electronics-only supply rails, or benchtop tool controllers. At 100W / 4.2A, it cannot sustain a standard 120W heated bed plus stepper load. Community context: sometimes used as a dedicated SBC + electronics PSU alongside a separate higher-wattage unit for the heated bed, cleanly isolating the two power domains.
Verdict Label: Compact accessory PSU — underpowered for full builds, correct for specific use cases
Cons:
100W / 4.2A cannot handle a standard 24V heated bed + stepper load simultaneously
Not suitable as primary PSU for Voron, RatRig, or any CoreXY with a standard heated bed
Temperature-controlled fan still present — not silent
Name: LRS-100-24
Pros:
Compact footprint — fits tight spaces where LRS-200-24 won’t
UL 62368-1 and CE certified — same reliability tier as larger LRS series
Inexpensive entry point
Good as secondary PSU for SBC + electronics, independent from heated bed supply

Description: Mean Well's 200W slim-line 24V supply (201.6W rated, 8.4A) in a 194 × 55 × 26 mm fanless metal case with 94% efficiency and active PFC. It cools silently by convection with no fan, but must be mounted to an aluminium plate or cabinet base to meet its derating curve. Suited to small printers and accessory loads rather than as a primary supply for a heated-bed build.
Verdict Label: Silent 200W supply for small builds and accessory loads — too small as a primary for heated-bed printers
Cons:
Only 201.6W — too small as a primary for heated-bed builds
Must be mounted to an aluminium plate to meet its derating curve
No DC OK signal or redundant function on the standard type
Name: UHP-200-24
Pros:
Silent fanless convection cooling, zero fan noise
Slim 26mm profile — 194 × 55 × 26 mm
94% efficient with built-in active PFC
UL 62368-1 certified

Description: The Mean Well NES-350-12 is a 348W enclosed single-output supply delivering 12V at up to 29A, with a built-in temperature-controlled fan and UL60950-1 approval. It suits 12V accessories, LED loads and other 12V equipment, but it cannot serve as the main supply for a standard 24V printer. Input voltage is selectable 115/230V by switch, so the switch must be set correctly before use.
Verdict Label: A proven 12V accessory supply, not a main PSU for a 24V printer.
Cons:
12V only — cannot power a standard 24V printer mainboard, heaters or motors
Fan-cooled, so not silent and the fan is a wear item
115/230V input selector switch must be set correctly before use
Older economy design at ~83% efficiency, below modern LRS/UHP units
Name: NES-350-12
Pros:
348W / 29A at 12V, plenty for 12V accessories and LED loads
UL60950-1 approved, with overload, over-voltage and over-temperature protection
Built-in fan with temperature-controlled on/off, output adjustable 10–13.5V

Description: For larger beds, enclosure/chamber heating, or higher total system draw where the 350W unit runs too close to its ceiling. A 350mm+ DC bed, an active chamber heater, or an AWD/toolchanger stepper count can pull the continuous load toward or past 350W; the LRS-600-24 restores headroom so the supply is not running near its limit. Same 24V rail and same Mean Well LRS reliability — just more margin.
Verdict Label: The big LRS - 600W of enclosed 24V power for high-draw builds.
Cons:
No verified USD price or Digi-Key listing found - buy carefully
Fan-cooled, not fanless
Overkill for most printers - the LRS-200-24 is the Voron BOM standard
No printer BOM ties this unit to a specific printer
Name: LRS-600-24
Pros:
600W rated output - the highest-wattage LRS in the table
Enclosed metal case, UL 62368-1 approved
Built-in fan with ON/OFF control - only runs when hot (on at 50C, off at 40C)
24V/25A single output from the most common printer-PSU series

Description: The Mean Well LRS-200-24 is the BOM-specified PSU for Voron 2.4 and Trident 250mm builds. It outputs 24V at up to 8.4A (200W) through a temperature-controlled internal fan that stays nearly silent at typical print loads. UL 62368-1 and CE certified. If you have a 250mm build with no heated chamber, this is the right PSU — no deliberation required.
Verdict Label: Voron BOM standard — the correct spec for 250mm heated bed builds
Cons:
200W headroom gets tight when adding heated chamber + accessories
Fan audible under sustained full load
Not right-sized for 300mm or 350mm builds
Name: LRS-200-24
Pros:
Voron Design BOM-specified for all 250mm builds
UL 62368-1 and CE certified — industrial-grade reliability
Temperature-controlled fan quiet at typical print loads
Wide input range (90–264 VAC) — works worldwide
Thousands of successful Voron builds documented on this exact unit

Description: The Silverstone SST-ST30SF is an SFX-format 300W ATX PSU used in some VzBot builds where compact form factor is the priority. ATX PSUs output 12V as the primary rail (plus 5V and 3.3V auxiliaries), so most VzBot builds using this unit pair it with a dedicated 24V Mean Well for heated bed and main stepper power, using the ST30SF for the SBC, electronics, and low-voltage accessories. Non-modular cable routing requires care in the compact VzBot bay. Budget-tier SFX option. Scope: auxiliary ATX PSU for secondary 12V use, not a primary printer PSU.
Verdict Label: Budget SFX pick for VzBot — fits the compact bay, tradeoffs to know
Cons:
Non-modular — unneeded cables require management in tight VzBot bay
12V primary rail — requires step-up converter or secondary 24V PSU for heated bed and stepper power
300W ceiling limits expansion headroom
80+ Bronze is the lowest efficiency tier in this comparison
Not specified in any standard BOM — narrower community adoption
Name: SST-ST30SF
Pros:
SFX form factor fits VzBot electronics bay without modification
300W sufficient for VzBot SBC + electronics (separate 24V PSU handles heated bed)
80+ Bronze certified
UL certified — safe for enclosed printer use
Less expensive than SF750 or EVGA 650 GM

Description: The LRS-350-48 is Mean Well's enclosed 350.4W single-output supply, delivering 48V at up to 7.3A from a low-profile 215×115×30mm case for builders running 48V stepper setups. It carries UL 62368-1 certification and uses a temperature-controlled built-in fan that only switches on above 50°C.
Verdict Label: A proven 48V workhorse for 48V motor builds, but the wrong voltage for a standard 24V printer.
Cons:
48V is non-standard for most hobbyist printers — needs a 48V-capable board and drivers
Requires manual 115/230V input voltage selection by switch
Fan adds noise and a wear item under sustained load
Name: LRS-350-48
Pros:
48V at 7.3A for high-voltage stepper setups
UL 62368-1 certified
Temperature-controlled fan only runs when hot
Low-profile 30mm enclosed case, up to 89% efficient

Description: The EVGA SuperNOVA 650 GM is the mid-range SFX-L pick for VzBot builds — 80+ Gold efficiency, fully modular cables, and 650W headroom at a price above the budget ST30SF. SFX-L form factor is longer than SFX spec (100mm vs 63.5mm depth), so verify chassis clearance before ordering. Community considers the 650 GM a cleaner choice than the ST30SF due to modular cabling, making it easier to route only what you need in a compact electronics bay. Same 12V rail caveats apply — dedicated 24V supply still recommended for the heated bed. Scope: auxiliary ATX PSU for secondary 12V use, not a primary printer PSU.
Verdict Label: Modular SFX-L for VzBot — good value between ST30SF and SF750
Cons:
SFX-L form factor is longer than SFX (100mm deep vs 63.5mm) — confirm chassis fit before ordering
12V primary rail — same 24V adaptation requirement as other ATX units
EVGA exited the GPU market — long-term warranty support may be slower to navigate
Not widely stocked vs. Corsair — harder to find locally
Name: SuperNOVA 650 GM
Pros:
Fully modular — clean cable routing in compact enclosures, only run what you need
80+ Gold efficiency — good balance of heat and cost
650W / 54A on 12V rail — sufficient headroom for most VzBot configurations
Lower price than Corsair SF750 at comparable quality tier
UL certified

Description: The UHP-500-24 is Mean Well's ultra-high-density fanless PSU and the community's go-to for zero-noise builds. It outputs 24V at 20.8A (500W) with no internal fan, conducting heat through the chassis mounting surface. Requires deliberate enclosure design: the PSU must mount flush against a metal panel, which acts as the heatsink. Community consensus on Voron Discord is that the UHP is the premium silent-build spec — but not a drop-in replacement for LRS units. You must plan the thermal path or risk derating.
Verdict Label: Community pick for silent builds — 500W with zero fan noise
Cons:
MUST be chassis-mounted with solid metal contact — not suitable for floating or poorly ventilated installs
Requires deliberate thermal design in electronics enclosure
More expensive than RSP-500-24 at equivalent wattage
Will derate under sustained full load without adequate chassis heatsinking
Name: UHP-500-24
Pros:
Completely silent — no fan, no noise under any load
500W / 20.8A — adequate for 350mm builds and heated chambers
Slim 40mm profile fits compact electronics bays cleanly
UL 62368-1 and CE certified
Heat conducts to chassis — PSU enclosure acts as heatsink

Description: The RSP-500-24 is the choice for 350mm Voron 2.4 builds or any build running a heated chamber alongside a large heated bed. At 500W / 20.8A, it delivers full rated output without derating under sustained multi-load conditions. Like the LRS series, the RSP uses a temperature-controlled fan (ON/OFF controlled, off below ~40°C) — consistently at full power, but audible under sustained load. PFC is included, making it cleaner on noisy or international mains supply.
Verdict Label: 350mm+ and heated chambers — full headroom, no derating
Cons:
Fan is audible under sustained load — not quiet-build friendly
Larger physical footprint than LRS series — requires more enclosure space
Overkill for 250mm or 300mm builds without chamber heating
Name: RSP-500-24
Pros:
500W / 20.8A — handles 350mm bed, chamber heater, and 5 steppers simultaneously
UL 62368-1 and CE certified
Forced-air cooling maintains full rated output at ambient temps
Active PFC — cleaner operation on noisy or international mains

Description: The Mean Well RS-50-5 is an enclosed 50W supply delivering 5V at up to 10A, cooled silently by free air convection with no fan. It is UL62368-1 approved and gives a Raspberry Pi or other 5V setup twice the current headroom of the 25W RS-25-5, but it is an accessory supply only — it cannot power a printer's 24V system.
Verdict Label: A silent 50W 5V supply with real headroom for a Pi plus 5V accessories.
Cons:
5V only, useless as a printer main PSU
Still only 50W — not a substitute for a 24V main supply
Mains-voltage screw terminals need a proper enclosure and careful wiring
Name: RS-50-5
Pros:
Fanless, silent free-air convection cooling
UL62368-1 approved, with short-circuit / overload / over-voltage protection
50W / 10A — double the RS-25-5, enough for a Pi plus 5V fans, LEDs or logic
Compact 99×97×36 mm, −25 to +70°C working range, under 0.5W no-load consumption

Description: Mean Well's 350W slim-line 24V supply (350.4W rated, 14.6A) in a 220 × 62 × 31 mm fanless metal case with 94% efficiency and active PFC. It cools silently by convection with no fan, but must be mounted to an aluminium plate or cabinet base to meet its derating curve. A direct silent replacement for a 350W LRS in a 300mm build.
Verdict Label: Silent 350W primary for 300mm builds with zero fan noise
Cons:
Must be mounted to an aluminium plate to meet its derating curve
Derates above ~45°C at 230VAC input
No DC OK signal or redundant function on the standard type
Name: UHP-350-24
Pros:
Silent fanless convection cooling, zero fan noise
350.4W / 14.6A at 24V — enough for a 300mm build
Slim 31mm profile — 220 × 62 × 31 mm
94% efficient with built-in active PFC
UL 62368-1 certified

Description: The LCP300-24D5 is LDO's compact, fully enclosed 300W dual-output power supply designed for 3D printing, delivering 24V across three terminals plus a 5V output from a single 120×95×35mm unit. Its GaN design with power factor correction runs at up to 91% efficiency, and dual AC input terminals let additional AC loads daisy-chain through the supply.
Verdict Label: A compact dual-output 24V+5V supply purpose-built for 3D printers, with no separate 5V supply needed.
Cons:
No UL certification — EN IEC 62368-1 LVD compliance only
5V rail is a buck converter off the 24V rail, max 25W
Gets hot at full 300W and needs external airflow
Narrow operating temperature range, -20 to 40°C
Name: LCP300-24D5
Pros:
Dual 24V (x3) + 5V outputs from one compact enclosed unit
GaN design with PFC, up to 91% efficient
Daisy-chainable dual AC input terminals simplify wiring
Overload, overvoltage and temperature protection built in

Description: The Mean Well RS-25-5 is a compact enclosed 25W supply delivering 5V at up to 5A, cooled silently by free air convection with no fan. It is UL62368-1 approved and well suited to powering a Raspberry Pi, Klipper host or other small 5V logic loads, but it has no role as a printer main supply.
Verdict Label: A compact silent 5V supply for a Raspberry Pi or other small 5V loads.
Cons:
Only 25W / 5A — one small 5V load, no headroom for more
5V only, useless as a printer main PSU
Mains-voltage screw terminals need a proper enclosure and careful wiring
Name: RS-25-5
Pros:
Fanless, silent free-air convection cooling
UL62368-1 approved, with short-circuit / overload / over-voltage protection
Compact 78×51×28 mm, wide −20 to +70°C working range, under 0.5W no-load consumption
3-year warranty

Description: The LRS-350-24 is the recommended PSU for 300mm Voron 2.4 and Trident builds, and the sensible upgrade for 250mm builds that add a chamber heater or substantial accessory load. Outputs 24V at up to 14.6A (350W) in the same mounting footprint as the LRS-200-24. Community consensus: spec the 350W over the 200W for any build running a PTC or silicone bed heater with simultaneous chamber heating — you never want to hit the ceiling under combined loads.
Verdict Label: Right-sized for 300mm builds and accessory-heavy configs
Cons:
Overkill for a stock 250mm build with no chamber heater
Fan noisier than LRS-200-24 at sustained high loads
Slightly more expensive than the 200W unit
Name: LRS-350-24
Pros:
Headroom for 300mm bed, chamber heater, and stepper load simultaneously
Same mounting footprint as LRS-200-24 — drop-in upgrade
UL 62368-1 and CE certified
Temperature-controlled fan stays quiet at moderate loads
Community-recommended upgrade path for 250mm builds adding a chamber heater
